title: Amaravati Takes Shape as India's Newest Capital With Rs 56,000 Crore Push
excerpt: Andhra Pradesh's greenfield capital city is rising from farmland with massive infrastructure investment, Singapore partnership, and a legally cemented status as the state's sole capital — targeting completion by March 2028.
body:
• Andhra Pradesh has launched Rs 56,000 crore in projects for Amaravati, with tenders worth Rs 50,552 crore issued and 74 construction works underway
  • The Seed Access Road is nearing completion and seven national highways now connect to the capital region, with a railway line also being laid
  • Parliament passed the AP Reorganisation Amendment Act in April 2026, legally establishing Amaravati as the state's sole capital with presidential assent
  • CM Naidu has secured Singapore's partnership for urban planning and attracted major institutions including VIT, SRM, BITS Pilani, and NID to the capital region

From Farmland to Capital City

On the banks of the Krishna River in Andhra Pradesh, one of India's most ambitious urban projects is taking shape. Amaravati, the greenfield capital city that CM N. Chandrababu Naidu has championed for over a decade, is entering an accelerated construction phase backed by Rs 56,000 crore in state investment and renewed political certainty.

https://x.com/Telugu360/status/2087811611545493949

The Seed Access Road — the arterial route connecting the capital's core government district — is nearing completion. Seven national highways now link to the Amaravati region, and a railway line is being laid to connect the capital to the broader transport network. Monthly progress reviews and real-time monitoring are in place, with contractors and officials warned of accountability if timelines slip.

Legal Certainty After Years of Limbo

Amaravati's status as Andhra Pradesh's sole capital was legally cemented in April 2026 when Parliament passed the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill. The legislation, which received President Droupadi Murmu's assent and was published in the Gazette, amended the original 2014 Act to insert the clause: "Amaravati shall be the new capital."

The move ended years of uncertainty. After Naidu first proposed Amaravati as the capital in 2014, his successor YS Jagan Mohan Reddy scrapped the plan and proposed three separate capitals — administrative in Visakhapatnam, legislative in Amaravati, and judicial in Kurnool. Construction stalled for five years under the YSRCP government, which dismissed the project as a "graveyard and a desert."

"Some people called Amaravati a graveyard and a desert, but we will turn it into the most liveable city in three years."

— N. Chandrababu Naidu, Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh

The Land Pooling Model

Amaravati's foundation rests on an unconventional approach to land acquisition. Rather than compulsory purchase, Naidu turned to land pooling — a model where farmers voluntarily contributed their agricultural land in exchange for developed plots and annual annuity payments. Under this arrangement, 29,000 farmers gave 33,000 acres across 23 villages in Guntur district.

A second phase of land pooling is now underway, with farmers contributing an additional 16,000 acres. Naidu has called the arrangement a "gamechanger," pointing to rising land values as validation that the farmers' bet on the capital is paying off.

Singapore Partnership and Global Ambitions

Singapore has been central to Amaravati's planning from the start. Jurong International and Surbana International developed the original master plans — a capital region concept for 7,420 square kilometers, a city master plan for 217 square kilometers, and a detailed seed capital plan for 16.9 square kilometers.

In a recent visit to Singapore, Naidu met Prime Minister Lawrence Wong to revive and deepen the partnership. He pitched Amaravati as a destination for semiconductor manufacturing, artificial intelligence research, and urban governance expertise. Wong sought details on the city's infrastructure progress and long-term development plan.

Major educational institutions are establishing campuses in the capital region, including VIT, SRM, NID, and BITS Pilani. The state is also developing Quantum Valley, a technology hub within Amaravati focused on quantum computing research, with Naidu projecting that quantum computers will be developed there within two years.

The Road to 2028

Naidu has set March 2028 as the target for completing the capital's core infrastructure — six months ahead of the original schedule. With Rs 15,000 crore in central government support and a coalition government at the Centre that counts Naidu's TDP as a key ally, the political conditions for Amaravati's construction are more favorable than they have been in a decade.

The capital is being designed as a blue-green city emphasizing sustainability, with net-zero targets, extensive green cover, electric vehicle promotion, and continuous air quality monitoring. If completed on schedule, Amaravati would join Gandhinagar, Chandigarh, Bhubaneswar, and Naya Raipur as one of independent India's planned state capitals — and potentially its most modern.
